review.tagline: Desktop, web and mobile front end for controlling local coding agent CLIs
review.summary: T3 Code is a control surface for coding agents already installed and authenticated on your machine: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode and Google Antigravity. It runs a local server started with the `t3` command and is reached through a web app, an Electron desktop app, or iOS and Android apps for remote use. The README says the project is early and bugs are expected.
review.audience: Developers who run several coding agent CLIs and want one local or remote UI
strengths: Drives six agent providers from one interface using your existing subscriptions
Clients for desktop (Electron), web, iOS and Android, with remote access to your machine
Installs via shell script, npx, winget, scoop, Homebrew, .deb or AUR
MIT licensed; can run as a background service with `t3 service install`
weaknesses: README says it is very early and to expect bugs
Mostly not accepting contributions; large features will not be merged
Needs at least one provider CLI installed and logged in beforehand
No docs site yet; docs are Markdown files in the repo
